name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Corpus Uteri
aliases: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Endometrium

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Corpus Uteri

criteria.description: Presence of malignant squamous cells with keratinization and intercellular bridges in endometrial tissue
Positive staining for cytokeratin markers (e.g., CK5/6, p63) confirming squamous differentiation
Exclusion of glandular differentiation or mixed histology to confirm pure squamous cell carcinoma
MRI or ultrasound showing uterine mass localized to corpus uteri

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant squamous cells with immunohistochemical evidence of squamous differentiation and exclusion of glandular components
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires biopsy and histopathological examination; imaging supports staging.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Malodorous vaginal discharge with necrotic tissue

common.symptomName: Pelvic pain localized to lower abdomen
searchTerms: pain in lower belly or pelvis

occasional.symptomName: Urinary frequency or urgency due to local invasion
Lower extremity edema from lymphatic obstruction
searchTerms: lower limb edema due to lymph obstruction
low red blood cells from bleeding
anemia due to chronic blood loss
abnormal opening between vagina and other organ

rare.symptomName: Lower limb neuropathy due to pelvic nerve involvement
searchTerms: leg numbness from pelvic nerve damage

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in advanced disease
imaging: MRI showing mass confined to corpus uteri with possible myometrial invasion
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; possible association with TP53 mutations in some cases
other: Histopathology revealing keratinizing squamous cells with intercellular bridges
Immunohistochemical positivity for p63 and CK5/6

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of glandular differentiation on histology
Positive staining for estrogen and progesterone receptors
More common presentation with abnormal uterine bleeding but different histopathology
Tumor origin at the cervix rather than corpus uteri
HPV association and positive HPV DNA testing
Different clinical staging and treatment protocols

redFlags: Unexplained pelvic pain with systemic symptoms
references: Orphanet: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Corpus Uteri (ORPHA:213716)
WHO Classification of Tumours: Female Genital Tumours, 5th Edition
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Uterine Neoplasms
